title: Runbooks-as-data: policy-driven task runner for safe admin automation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We rely on a collection of ad-hoc admin scripts and manual runbooks for oncall and routine maintenance. These are brittle, often undocumented in a machine-readable way, and risky to execute without human review. Goal: Introduce a runbooks-as-data pattern and a policy-driven task runner that turns approved YAML/JSON runbooks into audited, idempotent task executions with safety gates, ephemeral credentials, and automatic dry-run verification. The runner should be suitable for: (1) oncall incident remediation templates, (2) scheduled maintenance tasks, and (3) self-serve admin utilities in the ops console.
proposed_solution: Create an 'ops-runner' service that consumes a runbook catalog (git-backed) where each runbook is a structured document (metadata + steps + inputs + rollback). Runbooks are validated by a policy engine (RBAC, SLO thresholds, blast-radius checks) before being compiled into an execution plan. Execution plan features: step-level idempotency tokens, KV-cache-aware batching for multi-host ops, ephemeral credentials issued via KMS/HSM integration, audit log entries to the console and centralized ELK, and toggles for dry-run / simulation mode. Integrate with the ops chatbot for interactive confirmations and automatic follow-up ticket creation on failures. Provide a templating layer for parameterized tasks and a sandbox API for testing. Include a mode to mark steps as 'non-automatable' to require manual confirmation. Quantify success by reduction in mean time to remediate (MTTR) for priority incidents and number of manual steps avoided.
acceptance_criteria: Ops-runner can import runbooks from the git catalog and validate them against policy rules
Execution creates structured audit events (schema v1) sent to logging pipeline
Ephemeral credentials issued for actions have TTLs < 1 hour and are rotated per run
Dry-run produces a simulated execution trace that matches real-run within tolerance
Ability to mark steps as 'manual' so the runner pauses and emits a confirmation link
Integration test demonstrating automated remediation for a throttled cache node reduces MTTR by >= 30% in test harness
milestones: 2025-02-14: Design review and threat model completion
2025-02-28: KMS integration and audit logging hookup
2025-03-05: End-to-end test with ops playbook and documentation
rollout_plan: Canary with two oncall engineers and one service for 2 weeks
Collect metrics: run success rate, MTTR, manual step count, false positives from policy checks
Gradual enablement for teams by tag; default to dry-run mode before full automation
Post-canary security review and sign-off before org-wide enablement
qa_and_validation: Unit tests for policy engine and step compiler
Fuzzing on templated inputs to catch injection risks
Chaos-runbook tests in staging to validate idempotency
Manual tabletop with SREs to verify human-in-loop flows
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-automation could cause cascading changes. Mitigation: default conservative policies, blast-radius checks, and circuit-breakers
Risk: Credential leakage. Mitigation: ephemeral creds, strict audit trails, vault/KMS-only issuance
Risk: Incorrect templates causing outages. Mitigation: require signed runbooks and gated promotion from test to canary catalogs
Risk: Policy false-positives blocking needed remediation. Mitigation: provide override workflow with audit and 2nd approver
